channel.title: Bloomberg — diagnostic source feed
channel.description: Diagnostic feed grouped by acquisition connector.

item.title: Poland Says Russian Drone Briefly Entered Its Airspace
item.description: A Russian drone briefly strayed into Polish airspace during nighttime attack on western Ukraine, Polish military said, just days after three Russian missiles crashed in the country.
item.dc:creator: Piotr Skolimowski

item.title: Indonesia Says Recent Singapore Gas Cuts Due to Pipeline Repairs
item.description: Indonesia said a recent decline in natural gas flows to Singapore was due to pipeline maintenance, moving the focus away from its rising domestic needs.
item.dc:creator: Benjamin Liu

item.title: Spain Election 2026: Angry Generation Feels Left Behind as Economy Booms
item.description: Housing crisis has fueled voter outrage ahead of Nov. 29 election
item.dc:creator: Laura Millan and Clara Hernanz Lizarraga

item.title: Most Germans Now Oppose Military Support for Ukraine, Poll Shows
item.description: A majority of Germans now oppose military aid for Ukraine, according to a new poll that shows support dropping significantly over the last year.
item.dc:creator: Kamil Kowalcze

item.title: Indonesia Ex-Police Chief Accused of Treason Over Protest Links
item.description: Indonesia identified former National Police chief Listyo Sigit Prabowo and five other current or former senior police officers as suspects in an alleged treason plot against President Prabowo Subianto, accusing some of helping mobilize anti-government demonstrations.
item.dc:creator: Chandra Asmara

item.title: Malaysia Eyes Other Countries for Rohingya After Turkey Says No
item.description: Malaysia will persist in seeking other Organisation of Islamic Cooperation countries willing to accept Rohingya refugees after Turkey rejected a proposal to take some now living in the country, Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim said.
item.dc:creator: Kok Leong Chan

item.title: China Space Program to Fly Pakistan Pilot as its First Foreigner
item.description: A Pakistani Air Force Pilot will blast off on China’s Shenzhou-24 spacecraft Wednesday, becoming the first foreign astronaut in the history of China’s manned space program and the latest symbol of deepening bilateral ties.
item.dc:creator: Bloomberg News

item.title: Singapore PM Talks Nvidia's Huang and Megaspeed Probes
item.description: Singapore Prime Minister Lawrence Wong says he does not want the city-state to be used as a route for companies seeking to circumvent US chip export controls. He also spoke about Megaspeed investigations and Nvidia's Jensen Huang in a press conference in Canberra, Australia with counterpart Anthony Albanese. (Source: ABC)

item.title: Prosecutors Say Omar Search Warrant Concerned Decades-Old Acts
item.description: Federal prosecutors investigating Representative Ilhan Omar told a judge they believe she committed crimes over a period stretching back decades before she entered Congress, newly released court records show.
item.dc:creator: Myles Miller

item.title: Singapore Won’t Be Conduit to Skirt US Chip Curbs, Wong Says
item.description: Prime Minister Lawrence Wong doesn’t want Singapore to be used as a route for companies seeking to circumvent US chip export controls, as authorities in the city-state investigate locally based firm Megaspeed over its purchases of Nvidia Corp. chips.
item.dc:creator: Philip J. Heijmans

item.title: Lula’s Fiscal Plan Clears Congress After Brazil Currency Tanks
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva’s plan to curb public spending passed through Brazil’s Congress just hours after the real weakened past the closely watched 6-per-dollar level, already a sign that investors doubt the measures can stabilize the country’s finances.
item.dc:creator: Daniel Carvalho and Giovanna Bellotti Azevedo

item.title: Venezuela Presidential Election Negotiations: Key Electoral Reform Lags
item.description: Venezuela’s government and a faction of the opposition agreed to overhaul rules governing political parties, but stopped short of mapping out a reform of the country’s electoral body, a key prerequisite for presidential elections.
item.dc:creator: Andreina Itriago

item.title: Nvidia Board Faces Questions After Huang Reinstatement
item.description: "Balance of Power" focuses on the intersection of politics and global business. On today's show, Rep. Madeleine Dean, a member of the House Foreign Affairs Committee that will question Jensen Huang behind closed doors on Dec. 1, says his return to Nvidia raises serious concerns over national security and corporate governance. Marc Short, former chief of staff to Vice President Mike Pence, says congressional scrutiny of Jensen Huang is unlikely to end with his December appearances, predicting Democrats will revisit the Nvidia controversy after taking control of Congress in January. Terry Haines, founder of Pangaea Policy, says Nvidia and its board face potentially prolonged scrutiny over Jensen Huang. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: South Korea Scrambles Jets as Russian Warplanes Near Airspace
item.description: South Korea scrambled fighter jets and briefly ordered residents of an island off its east coast to seek shelter after Russian warplanes approached its airspace, the latest in a string of similar incidents in the region as Moscow steps up the use of its military to test US allies.
item.dc:creator: Soo-Hyang Choi

item.title: Haines: Nvidia Board Better ‘Lawyer Up’
item.description: Terry Haines, founder of Pangaea Policy, says Nvidia and its board face potentially prolonged scrutiny over Jensen Huang. Haines, who helped run congressional investigations into Enron and WorldCom, expects board members to be called to testify “repeatedly” as lawmakers examine national security and corporate oversight. He speaks with Kailey Leinz and Joe Mathieu on Bloomberg’s "Balance of Power." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Short: Expect ‘A Lot of Huang Hearings’ Ahead
item.description: Marc Short, former chief of staff to Vice President Mike Pence, says congressional scrutiny of Jensen Huang is unlikely to end with his December appearances, predicting Democrats will revisit the Nvidia controversy after taking control of Congress in January. Short also calls President Trump’s intervention in Huang’s reinstatement a “dangerous precedent.” He speaks with Kailey Leinz and Joe Mathieu on Bloomberg’s "Balance of Power." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Rep. Dean on Huang: ‘This Will Not End Well for Him’
item.description: Rep. Madeleine Dean, a member of the House Foreign Affairs Committee that will question Jensen Huang behind closed doors on Dec. 1, says his return to Nvidia raises serious concerns over national security and corporate governance. “This will not end well for Mr. Huang,” Rep. Dean tells Kailey Leinz and Joe Mathieu on Bloomberg’s "Balance of Power." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Trump Wins New Chance to Ask Judge to Toss Hush Money Case
item.description: A US appeals court gave President Donald Trump another shot at getting his state case moved to federal court where he enjoys broad immunity from prosecution following a landmark Supreme Court ruling.
item.dc:creator: David Voreacos and Patricia Hurtado

item.title: Army Prepares for Detonation in Iowa After Court Ruling
item.description: The acting secretary of the Army said the service was preparing for a controlled detonation of hazardous materials stored at a facility in Iowa to go forward, hours after a US appeals court ruled in the Trump administration’s favor.
item.dc:creator: Courtney McBride

item.title: Prabowo Names Amran Sulaiman, Sugiono Nominees for Indonesia VP
item.description: Indonesian President Prabowo Subianto named cabinet members Andi Amran Sulaiman and Sugiono as candidates to replace former Vice President Gibran Rakabuming Raka, setting the stage for a parliamentary vote that could reshape the balance of political power in Southeast Asia’s largest economy.
item.dc:creator: Chandra Asmara and Rosalind Mathieson
